title: Doctor’s Assistant
text: And so, we arrived at an open area where the carcass of a giant dragon lay.
“It’s a total spectacle. I wonder what kind of face Ren would make if he found out…”
Right now, a line of adventurers has formed in front of the giant dragon’s carcass. “The dragon slain by the Sword Hero!” There’s even a villager holding a sign that reads, “For each scale…”
“Aren’t they already on their way to Zeltoble?”
“Maybe. There’s a land route and a sea route, right?”
“Given Ren’s pace, the sea route seems faster.”
We gazed at the dragon’s carcass while chatting like this. It looks like the horns and eyes are already gone. The teeth are missing, too. It does look a bit like a pitifully gnawed-on carcass.
“Ugh… it doesn’t look like the heart or anything was ripped out, but the entrails seem to still be inside, don’t they?”
“That’s true.”
“…It stinks.”
“Ugh… Bro, it stinks really bad in here.”
Keel and Filolial-sama, who have keen senses of smell, looked quite uncomfortable.
“Ugh… Well, it’s been a week since it was killed, so it’s bound to start rotting. We might want to warn them.”
Muttering that, my Father—still wearing his robe—went to warn the villagers. After all, we can’t let them figure out that he’s the Shield Hero.
“Excuse me, but regarding this dragon’s carcass… the internal organs are starting to rot, so I think you should cut it up as soon as possible.　It might cause some strange endemic disease.”
“…What are you talking about? If we do that, adventurers won’t come here anymore.”
“But…”

Perhaps seeing Father’s persuasion as a personal attack, the villager glared at him coldly with a displeased expression. Father tried to persuade him several times, but after a while, he returned with his shoulders slumped.
“No luck. They’re so blinded by greed they won’t listen to a word I say. Maybe their hygiene standards are just too lax? And if I force them to get rid of it, who knows what they’ll say…”
“Then I’ll burn it all down myself!”
“No, you absolutely can’t do that!”
My Father scolded me. But is it really okay to just leave it alone? Well, my Father did warn them, after all. If a problem arises, it’ll be their own fault.
“Just to be safe, I’ll issue a warning to the villagers too… but isn’t it a bit noisy over there?”

There’s a direction where a group of adventurers is trudging along. From the looks of it, they’re better dressed than your average adventurer. Would it be safe to assume they’ve already done a Class Up?
“Maybe they’re the adventurers looking for the dragon’s treasure I heard about at the tavern?”
“I suppose so.”
“The dragon’s treasure, huh…”
“You found some before, didn’t you, bro?”
“Yeah. We found quite a lot of it—it was a shame we couldn’t bring it all back to Melromarc. We left it with Lars-chan, though.”
“That cool-looking lady—I swear her eyes were glowing gold.”
Well, well—it seems my Father has been venturing out to all sorts of places lately, too. Well, dragons come in all shapes and sizes, so I suppose treasure is found from time to time.
“Should we try looking for some too?”
“From the way things look, haven’t they already found some?”
“Maybe so.”
My Father is watching the direction the adventurers are trudging off in.
“Well, let’s go check it out and see what it’s like. We’re here anyway.”
“Yeah! It feels a little weird, but let’s go check it out, bro!”
“Let’s go.”
And so, we made our way deeper into the area beyond the giant dragon’s carcass.

Once we got there, we came across a battle between the adventurers and… monsters that could be called the dragon’s minions, who were fighting relentlessly to defend their lair. As expected, since we’d ventured quite deep into the wilderness, it seemed ordinary adventurers couldn’t make it this far. After all, we’d run into monsters several times on our way here.
“Guh… We’ve been fighting like this day after day, and even without the boss, we still can’t break through the treasure’s defenses?”

He muttered something like that from a distance. To me and Father, they didn’t look all that powerful, though… Still, the monsters seemed to be quite exhausted. Their numbers were dwindling, one by one. The monster guarding the cave—presumably the last one—was slain by a few adventurers.
“All right! Everyone! The dragon’s treasure is right in front of us! Let’s go! We’re going to make this our village’s source of wealth!”

The leader of the adventurers… seems to be a young adventurer from a nearby village. The village’s emblem is marked here and there on his armor and sword, and given what he just said, it’s clear he was fighting for his village. With a shout of “Ooh!”, he and the adventurers he fought alongside entered the dragon’s lair.

Since there are quite a few dangerous monsters around, there are no longer any adventurers near us. I headed toward the dragon’s lair with my Father and the others. Inside the lair, the monsters seem to be trying to protect the eggs and treasure as if it were their last line of defense. However, they aren’t as strong as the monsters outside the lair, so they’re being driven out by the adventurers.
“Whoa! Dragon eggs! These’ll fetch a high price!”
“So they were hiding treasure after all. For the Sword Hero not to notice this—he’s really clueless.”
And so on—they’re all searching the area with eyes burning with greed. That’s right. Ren is clueless in many ways.
“Bro… I don’t like the look in those guys’ eyes.”
Keel snuggled up to my Father and gripped his cloak tightly.
“Did you just start remembering the scene of the village being ravaged?”
“……Yeah.”
“I see. Even though they’re monsters…… that’s a bit harsh, isn’t it? Especially since they didn’t even defeat the boss dragon themselves……”

I can’t help but agree with Father. The idea of trying to monopolize the treasure even though they didn’t defeat the boss themselves—it makes me want to throw up just watching it. This is the same mindset as a bunch of pigs. These guys are men, but I’m starting to feel like they look just like pigs to me.
“No, stop it—!”
Just as I was thinking that, from deeper inside the lair—beyond the group that was ransacking the treasure while brutally slaughtering the surviving monsters—a voice rang out.
“Please stop… I beg you! Don’t… don’t kill everyone! Dad… help me…”
It was a voice filled with deep anguish. Keel’s ears twitched sharply in response to the voice, and he stopped burying his face in Father’s cloak and turned around.
“Hey, there’s a Demi-Human kid in the dragon’s lair.”
“They were probably raising it to be raped. Let’s capture this one and sell it off, too.”
With unpleasant grins on their faces, the adventurers advanced step by step toward the voice, slaughtering monsters as they went.
“GAAAAAWWWW!”
A growl echoed from somewhere—perhaps a monster had survived.
“I won’t let that happen! This time… I’ll prove I can protect her!”
“Ah, Keel-kun!”
Shaking off Father’s attempt to stop him, Keel charged into the lair.
“Ugh, seriously… This is annoying, but I guess I have no choice!　Motoyasu, come too! Sakura and the others as well!”
“Got it.”
“Yeah.”
“Keel!”
Chasing after Keel, Father, me, Sakura, and Luna entered the den.
“W-what is this mutt?!”
“Woof woof!”

Keel barked at the adventurers and stood in front of the one leading the group, as if protecting something. It’s hard for us to see clearly because the adventurers behind us are blocking our view… but it seems Keel is trying to protect the monster and the person behind it who’s calling out.
“I won’t let anyone take this kid! Woof woof!”
The person calling for help seems to be muttering under their breath.
“What the hell is this mutt! Is it a Beastman!? What’s a filthy Beastman doing in a place like this!”
“Wait, that kid in the back looks like a Nuui too… If there’s a Nuui here, they must be connected to this. Might as well capture them and sell them off while we’re at it!”
“I said I won’t let you!”
It looks like Keel grabbed the arm of the adventurer who was reaching out and hurled him across the room. One of the adventurers was flung right toward us.
“Hey…!”
At that moment, my Father shouted loudly. The adventurers behind us turned around.
“What’s going on? Some weird dog’s been getting in our way. Don’t cause any more trouble—”
“That one’s mine. I’m the one who set it on you guys.”
In a menacing voice, my Father declared this while still wearing his robe. Most of the adventurers turned around to check.
“What? You say you set this mad dog on us!?”
“Yeah, since it looks like you were about to commit an act that can only be described as heinous.”
“What’s so heinous about that! We were just trying to capture a tainted Demi-Human—”

Just as they turned to glare, the adventurers’ eyes fell on Sakura-chan and Luna-chan in their Filolial Queen forms. After all, right now, only the Saints of the Divine Bird are accompanied by Filolial-sama in her Filolial Queen form. There isn’t a single adventurer here who doesn’t know about us—we’re the talk of Melromarc. In fact, many of them bought medicine before starting their climb, and some probably bought food as well.
“Hey, now that I look closely, isn’t that the dog working as a vendor in the Saints of the Divine Bird’s carriage!?”
“That’s right! I won’t stand for what you lot are trying to do! Woof woof! Grr…”
Keel is growling harder than ever before.

“So there you have it. I’m here to put a stop to your exploitation… Since you’re adventurers, I won’t complain about you trying to get your hands on the treasure in the dragon’s lair. But if there are people among that treasure, isn’t it the human thing to do to protect them? And you’re just going to sell them off?　Depending on the situation, maybe it’d be better not to sell medicine or food around here.”
“H-Holy One! Did I hear that right? We were planning to protect them. Besides, they’re being held captive by monsters.”
The adventurers quickly parted to let the Father see the speaker and Keel. From there, I looked toward where Keel was standing guard.
There… was the assistant to Filo-tan’s Doctor!
